Subject: Private deployment: air-gapped image delivery & update process

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. As discussed, Nordic Bank is moving forward with a physical delivery for the initial private deployment (production boundary: closed VPC, no outbound egress). We need to align on three things before we sign the procurement:

- Escrow custody window (how long the signed images are stored before transit).
- Transit SLA and tamper-evidence expectations (transport vendor requirements).
- Update authority matrix — who at Redwood can sign-off after transport and who at Nordic can perform acceptance tests.

Could you share a proposed minimal flow (manifest -> escrow -> transfer -> on-site install -> acceptance) and the documents you require from logistics for audit (signed manifest, chain-of-custody pdf, signed courier SLA)?

Anna (procurement) is cc'd for contract and billing questions.

Subject: Re: Private deployment: air-gapped image delivery & update process

Hi Petri / Anna — thanks, this is actionable. High level proposal below (we can iterate):

1) Build & Sign (Redwood)
- We will produce an image bundle (signed with our build key) and a machine-readable manifest.
- We sign the manifest and provide an initial SHA256 manifest hash.

2) Escrow (Redwood-managed holding)
- Redwood will push the signed bundle to an escrow vault for up to 7 days by default (customizable).
- Escrow entry includes time-stamped signature and HSM proof-of-possession metadata (we will provide the attestation report).

3) Transfer (3rd-party courier chosen by customer)
- Courier must provide sealed tamper-evident packaging and a chain-of-custody log signed at each handoff.
- Courier SLA: max 48 hours transit within EU; any deviations trigger immediate hold-and-audit.

4) On-site Handoff & Verification (Customer + Redwood engineer)
- On arrival, customer scans the manifest hash and sends an acceptance request to the Redwood on-call engineer.
- Redwood provides an on-site verification script (offline) that validates signatures and image checksums.

5) Acceptance Tests & Release
- Customer runs agreed acceptance tests (sanity + canary workloads). If green, customer signs the acceptance document and we mark the release as installed.

Required documents from logistics: signed_manifest_v2.pdf, courier_chain_of_custody.json (or csv), and courier SLA. We can accept a notarized courier SLA or a sealed logistic certificate from SealShip.

Next steps: Rishi, can you attach a minimal authority matrix and the offline verification steps we will provide? Marissa, can you prepare a short SLA variation offering (48h/72h/expedited) and the pricing delta?

I'll prepare a short redlineable statement of work once we have the courier SLA and the authority matrix.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Fri, May 1, 2026 at 11:03 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Next steps: Rishi, can you attach a minimal authority matrix and the offline verification steps we will provide?

Attached: authority_matrix.csv (column: role,redwood_sign_off,customer_accept_sign,contact_email) — quick summary inline below.

- Engineered Release Authorization (Redwood Release Lead) — approves signed image release from escrow (single Redwood sign-off required).
- Transport Release Authorization (Customer Security Lead) — customer must approve transfer authorization window prior to pickup.
- On-site Acceptance Authorization (Customer Ops Lead) — final acceptance after offline verification and acceptance tests.

Offline verification steps (scripted; run on disconnected host):
1) Verify signature of manifest (Redwood build key).
2) Compute SHA256 of each image and compare with manifest.
3) Validate HSM attestation token included in manifest metadata.
4) Run integrity-only boot (isolated hypervisor) and capture boot checksum.
5) Run agreed subset of acceptance tests (sanity endpoints) and produce acceptance report (signed).

Escalation path for mismatches: if checksum/signature mismatch -> immediate quarantine, forensic hash capture, and courier return.

I recommend we include an 'acceptance hold' clause: customer has 24 hours after verification to approve; beyond that Redwood will hold the image and start an investigation.

Attachment: authority_matrix.csv

- Expedited (3d escrow, 48h transit): +12% one-time logistics surcharge.
- Escrow-only (customer arranges courier): +0% (we provide signed manifest & HSM report).
